verses.text: Yahweh said to Noah, “Come with all of your household into the ship, for I have seen your righteousness before me in this generation.
You shall take seven pairs of every clean animal with you, the male and his female. Of the animals that are not clean, take two, the male and his female.
Also of the birds of the sky, seven and seven, male and female, to keep seed alive on the surface of all the earth.
In seven days, I will cause it to rain on the earth for forty days and forty nights. I will destroy every living thing that I have made from the surface of the ground.”
Noah did everything that Yahweh commanded him.
Noah was six hundred years old when the flood of waters came on the earth.
Noah went into the ship with his sons, his wife, and his sons’ wives, because of the floodwaters.
Clean animals, unclean animals, birds, and everything that creeps on the ground
went by pairs to Noah into the ship, male and female, as God commanded Noah.
After the seven days, the floodwaters came on the earth.

In the six hundredth year of Noah’s life, in the second month, on the seventeenth day of the month, on the same day all the fountains of the great deep were burst open, and the sky’s windows were opened.
It rained on the earth forty days and forty nights.
In the same day Noah, and Shem, Ham, and Japheth — the sons of Noah — and Noah’s wife and the three wives of his sons with them, entered into the ship —
they, and every animal after its kind, all the livestock after their kind, every creeping thing that creeps on the earth after its kind, and every bird after its kind, every bird of every sort.
Pairs from all flesh with the breath of life in them went into the ship to Noah.
Those who went in, went in male and female of all flesh, as God commanded him; then Yahweh shut him in.
The flood was forty days on the earth. The waters increased, and lifted up the ship, and it was lifted up above the earth.
The waters rose, and increased greatly on the earth; and the ship floated on the surface of the waters.
The waters rose very high on the earth. All the high mountains that were under the whole sky were covered.
The waters rose fifteen cubits  higher, and the mountains were covered.
All flesh died that moved on the earth, including birds, livestock, animals, every creeping thing that creeps on the earth, and every man.
All on the dry land, in whose nostrils was the breath of the spirit of life, died.

Every living thing was destroyed that was on the surface of the ground, including man, livestock, creeping things, and birds of the sky. They were destroyed from the earth. Only Noah was left, and those who were with him in the ship.
The waters flooded the earth one hundred fifty days.

footnotes.content: Yahweh speaks to Noah alone in the hearing of his household, calling him to 'come' into the ship. Long before the door is shut, God has already seen Noah's righteousness in that crooked generation. It is a mercy to know the call comes from the One who has first looked on us with grace.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Noah is told to gather by pairs and by sevens according to clean and unclean animals. Even in judgment, the Lord is making provision to keep a remnant and preserve life for the world to come. A man of faith learns to obey the smallest details when God gives them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The birds are not forgotten in the gathering; seven and seven are brought to keep seed alive on all the earth. God cares about the wings of heaven as much as the hooves on the ground. His mercy reaches beyond man to the whole order He made.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God gives Noah a week to finish, and then forty days and forty nights of rain to destroy every living thing He had made. Judgment is sure, but it comes after a patient warning. I have learned that the Lord is slow to strike and gives time to obey before the door closes.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Noah does everything Yahweh commanded him, not most of it and not in his own way. After a hundred years of building, this final act of obedience is quiet faithfulness. The ark was built by faith, and now it is entered by faith.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Six hundred years old, and Noah steps into the waters of judgment that will wash the world clean. Age is no barrier when the Lord calls a man to trust Him. Here is an old man walking by faith where the rest of his generation would not.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Noah enters with his sons, his wife, and his sons' wives because of the floodwaters. The family that walked with him in righteousness now walks with him into the only refuge God had provided. Salvation in this hour is found not alone, but with those the Lord has given to the faithful.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Clean and unclean, birds and creeping things all come as they were appointed to come. There is no scrambling for places; the Lord is bringing His own to the refuge He has prepared. What God orders comes exactly as He said it would.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Pairs go in, male and female, just as God commanded Noah. The same God who joined them in the beginning now keeps them to go through the judgment and to fill the earth again. His faithfulness covers the smallest creatures as well as the great.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: After seven days, the floodwaters come exactly as Yahweh said they would. The week of waiting was not wasted; it was the last mercy before the deluge. God keeps His word in judgment as surely as He does in promise.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The date is exact: the six hundredth year of Noah, second month, seventeenth day. On that day the fountains of the great deep burst open and the windows of the sky were opened. The earth that God once separated with a firmament is now undone, returning in part to the waters it was drawn from.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: It rained forty days and forty nights without ceasing. The sky pours down what it had withheld, and the hidden depths pour up what had been shut away. I know a heart can be both broken by judgment and yet see the hand of God doing all He has said.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: On that very same day, Noah and his whole family enter the ship. God had given the warning, Noah had obeyed, and now the refuge is full just in time. There is comfort in the phrase 'on the same day' - the Lord's timing is neither late nor early.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Every kind comes as appointed - livestock, creeping things, birds of every sort. The order of creation is preserved in the preservation of the remnant. The God who made all things is careful to keep all things He means to keep.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Pairs with the breath of life go in to Noah. They do not come by accident; they come because the God who gives breath is merciful to give refuge to those with breath. Even the smallest sparrow is known to the One who shuts them safely in.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They go in male and female as God commanded, and then Yahweh shuts him in. Noah built the door, but only the Lord can shut it in mercy and in judgment. I am glad to know our final refuge is not our own hand on the latch, but the faithfulness of God Himself.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The flood comes for forty days as God said. The waters increase and lift the ship high above the earth. What once would have crushed the wood now bears up the remnant because the Lord ordained it to float.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The waters rise and increase greatly, and the ship floats on the surface. While the world is being undone beneath it, the little vessel rides on the very waters of judgment. There is a picture here: refuge is not escape from the storm, but being safe in it by God's appointment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The waters rise very high until all the high mountains under the whole sky are covered. The proud peaks that seemed unmovable are now hidden beneath the deep. Every refuge of man is washed away, and only the refuge God provided remains.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Fifteen cubits higher still, and the mountains are covered. The waters go far above the highest places of the earth. When God judges, there is no mountain high enough to flee to apart from the place He has ordained for refuge.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All flesh dies that moved on the earth - birds, livestock, animals, creeping things, and every man. The same breath the Lord gave is returned to Him in judgment. It sobers an old man to remember how holy is the God who gives life and takes it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All on the dry land in whose nostrils was the breath of the spirit of life died. The Lord marks the difference precisely - those with the breath of life outside the ark perished; those inside, preserved by His mercy. Life and death hang on the place of refuge.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Every living thing on the surface of the ground was destroyed, and only Noah and those with him in the ship were left. Readers today hear an echo of a greater rescue: just as God once shut Noah in to be saved through judgment, He has provided another refuge through whom all who flee to Him are kept safe. As of 2026-10, I am grateful that our rescue is not by a wooden ark, but by the One who bore the judgment for us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The waters flooded the earth one hundred fifty days. The judgment was thorough, but it was not endless; it had its appointed measure from the Lord. Even in the longest flood of wrath, the God who judges is the same God who will remember mercy.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
